test_intent: Verifies ChatLinkFormatter.GetChatLink returns bold markdown for a chat with positive ID and no username (channel-like).
reason: Clean focused unit test with exact string assertion against a pure utility. No external dependencies, no mocks, direct instantiation. Asserts meaningful formatting behavior for channels without usernames.

test_intent: Verifies that when a chat has a null title, the formatter substitutes a Russian default title and still produces a valid markdown link.
reason: Meaningful edge-case test for null title handling. Exact string assertion verifies both the default title substitution and correct link formatting. Pure unit test with no external dependencies.

test_intent: Verifies that when a chat has an empty string title, the formatter produces empty brackets in the markdown link.
reason: Documents current behavior for empty title edge case. The behavior (empty brackets) is arguably questionable UX, but the test itself is clean and correctly asserts the current contract. Low value because empty title is rare in practice, but keeping it as behavioral documentation is harmless.

test_intent: Verifies that markdown special characters (*, _, [, ]) in chat titles are properly escaped in the formatted link output.
reason: Critical test for markdown escaping correctness. Unescaped markdown in chat links would break Telegram message formatting. Exact string assertion covers multiple special characters. Pure unit test with no external dependencies.

test_intent: Verifies that TelegramBotClientWrapper constructor throws ArgumentNullException when passed a null TelegramBotClient.
reason: Clean defensive programming test verifying constructor null guard. Uses Assert.Throws with exact exception type. No meaningful external dependency despite creating real TelegramBotClient instances elsewhere in the fixture. The test itself only exercises the null path.

test_intent: Verifies that TelegramBotClientWrapper.BotId correctly extracts the numeric bot ID from the Telegram bot token.
reason: Tests a real production behavior (token ID extraction) with exact assertion. Moderate maintenance risk because it instantiates a real TelegramBotClient with a hardcoded fake token, which depends on SDK token parsing behavior. The assertion itself is meaningful and the test is focused.

test_intent: Verifies that TelegramBotClientWrapper constructor throws ArgumentNullException when passed a null TelegramBotClient.
reason: Exact duplicate of TelegramBotClientWrapper_Constructor_ThrowsOnNullBot in the same test class. Both tests invoke the same assertion: Assert.Throws<ArgumentNullException> with null as the first constructor argument. No distinct bot contract exists beyond what the other test already covers.

test_intent: Verifies ChatLinkFormatter.GetChatLink returns a markdown link for a public group with a username.
reason: Exact duplicate of the same test in StatisticsServiceGetChatLinkTests. Both test files instantiate ChatLinkFormatter directly and assert identical behavior (public group with username produces markdown link). The behavior is already covered by the StatisticsServiceGetChatLinkTests variant. WorkerGetChatLinkTests appears to be a near-complete copy of the other test class.
